title: Text, statutory structure, and legislative context
shortTitle: Text, statutory structure, and legislative context
summary: Statutory context consists of surrounding provisions, institutional design, and other reliable information that bears on the meaning of disputed language.
notes:
Whitman reads the health-standard provision in its regulatory setting before assessing delegation. The Gundy plurality reads applicability language with the registration statute’s structure and purpose. Humphrey’s Executor uses the removal clause, tenure provisions, commission functions, and legislative history to identify intended independence.

These examples show why interpretation often precedes a structural constitutional question. They do not establish that every interpretive material has equal weight or that statutory purpose can displace any text. Whitman’s rejection of an unavailable cost-based reading supplies a limit, and Gundy’s disagreement shows that judges can dispute what the same context establishes.
